title: Foliation Holonomy and the Holonomy Groupoid

items.title: Local transversals to a regular foliation
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a regular foliation of codimension $q$ on a smooth $n$-manifold $M$, with tangent distribution $D=TF$. A subset $T\subseteq M$ is a **local transversal to $F$ at $x\in T$** when $T$ is an embedded submanifold of $M$ of dimension $q$ containing $x$ with $T_xM=D_x\oplus T_xT$. Equivalently $T_xT$ is a linear complement of $D_x$ in $T_xM$; because $\dim T=q=\operatorname{codim}F$, the sum condition is automatically direct. The definition is local: it is a condition at the single point $x$.
items.strategy: Specialise the published vocabulary: $F$ is a regular foliation atlas, and its tangent distribution $D$ is the smooth rank-$(n-q)$ subbundle supplied by the correspondence theorem. The tangent space $T_xT$ is that of an embedded submanifold, and $\operatorname{codim}F=q$. The dimension hypothesis $q$ is stated explicitly so that transversality is exactly the direct-sum condition and a codimension-one submanifold meeting a leaf tangentially is excluded. No choice principle is used beyond the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of the smooth-distribution setting.

references.title: Danny Calegari, Foliations and the Geometry of 3-Manifolds (Oxford Mathematical Monographs)
Leiden NCG seminar, Noncommutative Geometry of Foliations (2023 seminar notes)

items.title: Leafwise paths and leafwise homotopy relative to endpoints
items.statement: Let $F$ be a regular foliation of $M$. A **leafwise path** for $F$ is a continuous map $a:[0,1]\to M$ whose image is contained in a single leaf of $F$. A **leafwise homotopy relative to endpoints** between leafwise paths $a,b$ with the same endpoints $x,y$ is a continuous map $H:[0,1]^2\to M$ with $H(0,t)=a(t)$, $H(1,t)=b(t)$, $H(s,0)=x$ and $H(s,1)=y$ for all $s,t$, such that $t\mapsto H(s,t)$ is a leafwise path for every $s$. Leafwise homotopy relative to endpoints is an equivalence relation, and homotopic relative endpoints means equivalent in this relation. Continuity is in $M$; the leaf topology is not used.
items.strategy: Unpack the published relative-homotopy vocabulary on the square $I^2$ and the published notion of leaf. The only new clause is that every time-slice lies in a single leaf, which is what makes transverse transport well defined. Reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity are inherited from the published homotopy equivalence-relation results by keeping the leafwise condition at every stage; no topology finer than the topology of $M$ is introduced. The definition is choice-free.

references.title: Danny Calegari, Foliations and the Geometry of 3-Manifolds (Oxford Mathematical Monographs)
Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)
Leiden NCG seminar, Noncommutative Geometry of Foliations (2023 seminar notes)

items.title: Germs of local diffeomorphisms at a point
items.statement: Let $M,N$ be smooth manifolds and $x\in M$, $y\in N$. A **germ of local diffeomorphisms from $(M,x)$ to $(N,y)$** is an equivalence class of local diffeomorphisms $f:U\to V$ with $U$ open in $M$, $x\in U$, $V$ open in $N$, $y\in V$ and $f(x)=y$, two such being equivalent when they agree on some neighbourhood of $x$. When $M=N$ and $x=y$, write $\operatorname{Diff}_x(M)$ for the set of germs of local diffeomorphisms $(M,x)\to(M,x)$; composition of representatives makes $\operatorname{Diff}_x(M)$ a group, with identity the germ of $\mathrm{id}_M$ and inverse the germ of a local inverse.
items.strategy: The germ relation follows the published germ-of-smooth-maps pattern, restricted to local diffeomorphisms. Composition and inversion of representatives are well defined on germs and satisfy the group laws; this is proved as the next lemma, which is recorded as the well-definedness certificate (`justified_by`) of this definition. No choice principle is used.

references.title: Leiden NCG seminar, Noncommutative Geometry of Foliations (2023 seminar notes)
Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)

items.title: Germs of local diffeomorphisms at a point form a group
items.statement: With the notation of the preceding definition: composition of representatives induces a well-defined binary operation on $\operatorname{Diff}_x(M)$; this operation is associative, the germ of the identity is a two-sided identity, and every germ has a two-sided inverse. Hence $\operatorname{Diff}_x(M)$ is a group.
items.strategy: Well-definedness: if $f\sim f'$ and $g\sim g'$ as germs at $x$ with composable targets, restrict all four maps to a common neighbourhood of $x$ on which $f=f'$ and $g=g'$; then $f\circ g=f'\circ g'$ near $x$. Associativity is inherited from composition of maps on a common neighbourhood. Identity and inverses: the germ of $\mathrm{id}_M$, and for a local diffeomorphism $f$ the germ of its local inverse, which exists by the definition of a local diffeomorphism and the inverse function theorem. The group axioms are then checked on representatives; the source records exactly this statement.

references.title: Leiden NCG seminar, Noncommutative Geometry of Foliations (2023 seminar notes)
Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)

items.title: A leafwise path determines a germ of a transverse diffeomorphism
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $F$
be a regular foliation of a smooth manifold $M$, let $a$ be a leafwise path from
$x$ to $y$ ([[def-leafwise-path-and-leafwise-homotopy]]), let $T$ be a local
transversal to $F$ at $x$ and $T'$ a local transversal to $F$ at $y$
([[def-local-transversal-to-a-regular-foliation]]). Suppose
$0=t_0<\dots<t_N=1$ and foliation charts $U_1,\dots,U_N$ satisfy
$a([t_{i-1},t_i])\subseteq U_i$, and choose local transversals $T_i$ at
$a(t_i)$ for $i=1,\dots,N-1$ with $T_0=T$ and $T_N=T'$. Then the chart-wise
transports along plaques compose to a germ of a local diffeomorphism
$h_a:(T,x)\to(T',y)$, the **holonomy germ of $a$** along the displayed data
([[def-germ-of-a-local-diffeomorphism-at-a-point]]). Every leafwise path admits
such a finite chart chain, so every leafwise path together with its endpoint
transversals determines at least one such germ.
items.strategy: Compactness of $[0,1]$ and continuity of $a$ produce a finite chain of foliation charts. In a chart the plaques are the level sets of the transverse coordinates; the transport from $T_{i-1}$ to $T_i$ within $U_i$ keeps the transverse coordinates fixed and is a local diffeomorphism germ, because a transversal meets each nearby plaque in exactly one nearby point (transversality gives an invertible graph description, so the smooth inverse function theorem applies). Consecutive charts describe the same plaque germ through their common point by the published compatible-germs lemma, so the transports compose. The displayed auxiliary choices are recorded; their independence is the next lemma.

references.title: Danny Calegari, Foliations and the Geometry of 3-Manifolds (Oxford Mathematical Monographs)
Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)
Leiden NCG seminar, Noncommutative Geometry of Foliations (2023 seminar notes)

items.title: The holonomy germ is independent of the foliation chart chain
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. In the situation of the preceding lemma, the germ $h_a:(T,x)\to(T',y)$ depends only on the leafwise path $a$ and the endpoint transversals $T,T'$: it is unchanged by passing to a refinement of the chart chain, by changing the subdivision points, and by changing the auxiliary intermediate transversals $T_1,\dots,T_{N-1}$. Consequently $h_a=h_a(T',T)$ is a well-defined germ of a local diffeomorphism $(T,x)\to(T',y)$.
items.strategy: Two chains admit a common refinement by taking foliation charts through each point of the path and intersecting covers; along a common subinterval the plaque transports agree because overlapping plaques through a common point determine the same germ. Changing an intermediate transversal $T_i$ replaces the pair of consecutive transports by an equivalent composite: all maps involved keep the transverse coordinates of one common chart fixed, and composing the two descriptions gives the identity on a common neighbourhood. Both reductions are finite and local, and repeated comparison proves the assertion.

references.title: Danny Calegari, Foliations and the Geometry of 3-Manifolds (Oxford Mathematical Monographs)
Leiden NCG seminar, Noncommutative Geometry of Foliations (2023 seminar notes)
Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)

items.title: Holonomy depends only on leafwise homotopy relative to endpoints
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $F$
be a regular foliation of $M$, let $a,b$ be leafwise paths from $x$ to $y$ that
are leafwise homotopic relative to endpoints
([[def-leafwise-path-and-leafwise-homotopy]]), and let $T,T'$ be local
transversals at $x$ and $y$ ([[def-local-transversal-to-a-regular-foliation]]).
Then $h_a(T',T)=h_b(T',T)$ as germs. In particular the holonomy germ of a
leafwise path depends only on its leafwise homotopy class relative to endpoints
and on the endpoint transversals.
items.strategy: Subdivide the unit square into finitely many small rectangles each mapped by the homotopy into a single foliation chart: continuity on the compact square gives a uniform subdivision. In one chart, replace the homotopy on a rectangle by its two boundary paths; the two boundary paths from the same point to the same point differ only within one plaque, and the coordinate computation shows that they induce the same plaque transport. Chaining these replacements over the finitely many rectangles replaces $a$ by $b$ step by step, and the chain-independence lemma makes each replacement leave the endpoint germ unchanged. Hence $h_a=h_b$.

references.title: Danny Calegari, Foliations and the Geometry of 3-Manifolds (Oxford Mathematical Monographs)
Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)
Leiden NCG seminar, Noncommutative Geometry of Foliations (2023 seminar notes)

items.title: Holonomy respects path concatenation and reversal
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $a$ be a leafwise path from $x$ to $y$, let $b$ be a leafwise path from $y$ to $z$, and let $T,S,R$ be local transversals at $x,y,z$. Then, with $a*b$ the concatenation (traverse $a$, then $b$), $h_{a*b}(R,T)=h_b(R,S)\circ h_a(S,T)$. Also $h_{a^{-1}}(T,S)=\bigl(h_a(S,T)\bigr)^{-1}$, where $a^{-1}$ is the reversed leafwise path.
items.strategy: Verify first in a single foliation chart: concatenating two paths contained in one chart composes the plaque transports, and reversing a path inverts the local diffeomorphism, because the plaque transport within a chart is the same map read in the two directions. The general case follows by refining a chart chain for $a*b$ so that it contains chains for $a$ and $b$ meeting at the middle transversal $S$, and then applying the chain-independence lemma; inverses of germs exist by the germ-group lemma.

references.title: Danny Calegari, Foliations and the Geometry of 3-Manifolds (Oxford Mathematical Monographs)
Leiden NCG seminar, Noncommutative Geometry of Foliations (2023 seminar notes)
Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)

items.title: The holonomy representation and the holonomy group of a leaf
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $F$
be a regular foliation of $M$, let $L$ be a leaf
([[def-leaf-of-a-regular-foliation]]), let $x\in L$, and let $T$ be a local
transversal to $F$ at $x$ ([[def-local-transversal-to-a-regular-foliation]]).
Equip $L$ with the unique intrinsic smooth manifold structure of its maximal connected integral manifold of $TF$ ([[thm-regular-foliations-and-integrable-distributions-correspond]], [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-maximal-connected-integral-manifolds]]). This topology, rather than the ambient subspace topology, defines $\pi_1(L,x)$. The leaf inclusion is smooth and continuous, so intrinsic leaf loops and endpoint-fixed homotopies are leafwise paths and homotopies in $M$.

Since $T$ is a smooth manifold, the germs at $x$ of local diffeomorphisms
$T\to T$ form the group $\operatorname{Diff}_x(T)$
([[def-germ-of-a-local-diffeomorphism-at-a-point]],
[[lem-germs-of-local-diffeomorphisms-form-a-group]]).

The **holonomy representation of $L$ at $x$ relative to $T$** is
$$\rho_x:\pi_1(L,x)\to\operatorname{Diff}_x(T),\qquad \rho_x([a]):=h_{a^{-1}}(T,T),$$
where $a$ is a based loop in the intrinsic leaf topology
([[def-based-loops-and-fundamental-group]],
[[def-leafwise-path-and-leafwise-homotopy]]). The inverse is essential:
the library product $[a][b]=[a*b]$ traverses $a$ first, whereas ordinary
composition of germs applies the rightmost map first. Homotopy invariance
and reversal therefore give
$\rho_x([a][b])=(h_b\circ h_a)^{-1}=h_a^{-1}\circ h_b^{-1}
=\rho_x([a])\circ\rho_x([b])$
([[thm-holonomy-depends-only-on-leafwise-homotopy-relative-endpoints]],
[[lem-holonomy-respects-path-concatenation-and-reversal]]).
Thus $\rho_x$ is a homomorphism. The unreversed map $[a]\mapsto h_a(T,T)$
is an antihomomorphism with the same image and kernel. The **holonomy
group** of $L$ at $x$ is the image
$$\operatorname{Hol}(L,x):=\rho_x\bigl(\pi_1(L,x)\bigr)\le\operatorname{Diff}_x(T),$$
a subgroup of the group of germs in the sense of [[def-subgroup]] and
[[def-group]].

Replacing $T$ by another local transversal $T_1$ at $x$ replaces $\rho_x$ by a
conjugate homomorphism: with $\alpha$ the germ of the transport across the
plaque at $x$ from $T_1$ to $T$, one has
$\rho_x^{T_1}([a])=\alpha^{-1}\circ\rho_x^{T}([a])\circ\alpha$ for every leaf
loop $a$. Indeed, viewing the loop $a$ as the concatenation of the constant path
at $x$, then $a$, then the constant path at $x$, the concatenation law gives
exactly this formula, with the constant-path germs supplying $\alpha$ and
$\alpha^{-1}$ ([[lem-holonomy-respects-path-concatenation-and-reversal]]). It
follows that the kernel of $\rho_x$ and the conjugacy class of the holonomy
group are intrinsic to the leaf and do not depend on the choice of the local
transversal $T$. The representative $\rho_x$ itself does depend on $T$.
items.strategy: Give the leaf its unique intrinsic integral-manifold structure under Countable Choice. Its continuous inclusion turns intrinsic paths and homotopies into leafwise ones. Since loop multiplication traverses a first and then b whereas germ composition applies the rightmost map first, use rho([a])=h_(a inverse) to obtain a homomorphism. The image and kernel agree with those of forward holonomy, and constant-path transports give conjugacy when the endpoint transversal changes. No choice beyond the standing AC_omega is used.

references.title: Leiden NCG seminar, Noncommutative Geometry of Foliations (2023 seminar notes)
Danny Calegari, Foliations and the Geometry of 3-Manifolds (Oxford Mathematical Monographs)
Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)

items.title: The deck group of a connected covering acts by a covering-space action
items.statement: Let $p:E\to B$ be a covering map with connected total space $E$. Then the deck group $\operatorname{Deck}(p)$ acts on $E$ by a covering-space action: every $e\in E$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ with $hU\cap U=\varnothing$ for every nonidentity $h\in\operatorname{Deck}(p)$.
items.strategy: Take an evenly covered neighbourhood $W$ of $p(e)$ and let $U$ be the sheet of $p^{-1}(W)$ containing $e$. Every deck transformation maps sheets over $W$ onto sheets over $W$. If $hU=U$, then $h$ carries the unique point of $U$ over $p(e)$ to itself, so $h=\mathrm{id}$ by one-point determination on the connected total space. Hence for $h\ne\mathrm{id}$ the sheets $hU$ and $U$ are distinct, and distinct sheets over $W$ are disjoint. Thus $hU\cap U=\varnothing$.

references.title: Danny Calegari, Foliations and the Geometry of 3-Manifolds (Oxford Mathematical Monographs)
Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)

items.title: The covering of a leaf associated with the holonomy kernel exists
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a regular foliation, $L$ a leaf with base point $x$, $T$ a local transversal at $x$, $\rho_x:\pi_1(L,x)\to\operatorname{Diff}_x(T)$ the holonomy representation and $K=\ker\rho_x$. Then there is a connected covering $p:\widehat L\to L$ with $p_*\pi_1(\widehat L,\hat x)=K$ for a point $\hat x$ over $x$: take the universal cover $\widetilde L\to L$, identify $\pi_1(L,x)$ with its deck group, and put $\widehat L:=\widetilde L/K$. Moreover any two connected coverings of $L$ with image subgroup $K$ are isomorphic over $L$.
items.strategy: The leaf $L$ carries its smooth manifold structure, so it is nonempty, path-connected, locally path-connected and semilocally simply connected (charts map to convex Euclidean sets), hence has a universal cover. The deck group of that cover is $\pi_1(L,x)$ and acts by a covering-space action; restricting to the subgroup $K$ keeps the covering-space property, so the orbit map $\widetilde L\to\widetilde L/K$ is a covering whose deck group is $K$ (the acting group), and $\widetilde L$ is simply connected, so $\pi_1(\widehat L)\cong K$ with image exactly $K$ under $p_*$. Uniqueness is the covering-space lifting criterion applied in both directions, using the universal cover's dominating property.

references.title: Leiden NCG seminar, Noncommutative Geometry of Foliations (2023 seminar notes)
Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)

items.title: The holonomy cover of a leaf
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a regular foliation, $L$ a leaf with base point $x$, $T$ a local transversal at $x$, $\rho_x$ the holonomy representation and $K=\ker\rho_x$. The **holonomy cover** of $L$ (relative to $T$) is the connected covering $p:\widehat L\to L$ with $p_*\pi_1(\widehat L,\hat x)=K$ supplied by the preceding lemma, equipped with a base point $\hat x$ over $x$; it is unique up to a unique isomorphism over $L$. By construction $\pi_1(\widehat L,\hat x)\cong K$ and $p$ is a covering of $L$ by the holonomy orbits of $\rho_x$.
items.strategy: Definition by the existence-and-uniqueness lemma: the object is the covering attached to the kernel of the holonomy representation, so no further construction is needed. The kernel is independent of the choice of $T$ because replacing $T$ conjugates $\rho_x$. This is the leaf-level input for the finite-holonomy normal model of the Reeb stability pair, which consumes the holonomy cover, not the universal cover.

references.title: Leiden NCG seminar, Noncommutative Geometry of Foliations (2023 seminar notes)
Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)

items.title: The monodromy groupoid of a foliation
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a regular foliation of $M$. The **monodromy groupoid** $\operatorname{Mon}(F)$ is the groupoid with object set $M$ whose arrows from $x$ to $y$ are the leafwise homotopy classes relative to endpoints of leafwise paths from $x$ to $y$ (there is no arrow when $x,y$ lie in different leaves). Composition is induced by concatenation of leafwise paths, the identity at $x$ is the class of the constant path, and inverses are induced by path reversal. These operations are independent of representatives by the published homotopy results. The groupoid is set-theoretic: no topology is imposed and no smooth structure on the arrow set is asserted.
items.strategy: The arrow set is the quotient of the set of leafwise paths by leafwise homotopy relative to endpoints, an equivalence relation by the preceding definition. Composition of classes is well defined because homotopies compose, associativity holds up to the standard reparametrisation homotopy, the constant path is a two-sided identity, and reversal is a leafwise path giving the inverse class. Only set-theoretic structure is claimed here; the smooth/étale structure is not constructed on this page.

references.title: Leiden NCG seminar, Noncommutative Geometry of Foliations (2023 seminar notes)
Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)

items.title: The holonomy groupoid of a foliation
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a regular foliation of $M$. Two leafwise paths with the same endpoints are **holonomy-equivalent** when their holonomy germs relative to one, equivalently by chain independence every, choice of local transversals at the endpoints agree. The **holonomy groupoid** $\operatorname{Hol}(F)$ is the groupoid with object set $M$ whose arrows are the holonomy classes of leafwise paths, with composition induced by concatenation. It is the quotient of the monodromy groupoid by the relation that identifies arrows with equal holonomy germs; arrows whose endpoints are not composable have no composite. The projection $\operatorname{Mon}(F)\to\operatorname{Hol}(F)$ sends a homotopy class to its holonomy class.
items.strategy: The relation refines leafwise homotopy relative to endpoints (homotopic paths have equal germs) and is independent of the phrase 'one, equivalently every' by chain independence. Composition of holonomy classes is well defined by multiplicativity of holonomy germs; the well-definedness of the quotient structure is proved as the next lemma, which is recorded as this definition's `justified_by` certificate. As with the monodromy groupoid, no topology on the arrow set is asserted here.

references.title: Leiden NCG seminar, Noncommutative Geometry of Foliations (2023 seminar notes)
Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)
Danny Calegari, Foliations and the Geometry of 3-Manifolds (Oxford Mathematical Monographs)

items.title: Holonomy classes form a groupoid congruence
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). On the
set of leafwise paths of $F$, the relation "same endpoints and equal holonomy
germs" is an equivalence relation coarser than leafwise homotopy relative to
endpoints, and it is a congruence for concatenation: if $a\sim a'$ and
$b\sim b'$, and $a*b$ and $a'*b'$ are defined, then $a*b\sim a'*b'$.
Consequently the quotient $\operatorname{Hol}(F)$ is a groupoid and the
projection $\operatorname{Mon}(F)\to\operatorname{Hol}(F)$ is a groupoid
morphism ([[def-holonomy-groupoid-of-a-foliation]],
[[def-monodromy-groupoid-of-a-foliation]]).
items.strategy: Equality of typed germs and homotopy invariance give an equivalence relation coarser than leafwise homotopy. For composable paths a then b, h_(a*b)=h_b composed with h_a; representative agreement on a source neighborhood whose image lies in the target agreement neighborhood proves that composition respects equality, even between different transversals. Equal diffeomorphism representatives have equal inverse representatives on their common image. The explicit monodromy homotopies give associativity, constant-path identities, and reversal inverses in the quotient.

references.title: Leiden NCG seminar, Noncommutative Geometry of Foliations (2023 seminar notes)
Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)

items.title: The isotropy of the holonomy groupoid is the leaf holonomy group
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a regular foliation, $x\in M$, $L$ the leaf through $x$, $T$ a local transversal at $x$ and $\rho_x:\pi_1(L,x)\to\operatorname{Diff}_x(T)$ the holonomy representation. Then the isotropy group $\operatorname{Hol}(F)(x,x)$ of the holonomy groupoid is canonically isomorphic to the holonomy group $\operatorname{Hol}(L,x)=\rho_x(\pi_1(L,x))$: the map sending the holonomy class of a leaf loop at $x$ to its holonomy germ is a group isomorphism. In particular the isotropy is trivial if and only if the holonomy representation is trivial.
items.strategy: Arrows $x\to x$ of $\operatorname{Hol}(F)$ are holonomy classes of leaf loops at $x$; by definition of the relation they are in bijection with their germs, and the germ of a loop is $\rho_x([a])$, so the map is a bijection onto $\rho_x(\pi_1(L,x))$. Multiplicativity of holonomy germs makes it a homomorphism: the class of the concatenation $a*b$ maps to $h_b\circ h_a$, which is the product of the images. Hence it is an isomorphism of groups, and vanishing of the image is equivalent to triviality of the representation.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)
Leiden NCG seminar, Noncommutative Geometry of Foliations (2023 seminar notes)

items.title: Smooth maps transverse to a regular foliation
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a regular foliation of $M$ with tangent distribution $D=TF$, let $N$ be a smooth manifold and $f:N\to M$ a smooth map. Then $f$ is **transverse to $F$ at $x\in N$** when $$df_x(T_xN)+D_{f(x)}=T_{f(x)}M,$$ and **transverse to $F$** when this holds at every $x\in N$. When $N\subseteq M$ and $f$ is the inclusion this is transversality of a submanifold to $F$; the condition forces $\dim N\ge\operatorname{codim}F$ at every point, and it is automatic when $\operatorname{codim}F=0$.
items.strategy: Specialise the published definition of transverse smooth maps to the case where the second map is the inclusion of the leaf distribution $D$, viewed as a smooth subbundle of $TM$ along the base map. All clauses are pointwise linear algebra in the tangent spaces, so the definition inherits the conventions of the published transversality vocabulary and adds no choice beyond the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

references.title: Danny Calegari, Foliations and the Geometry of 3-Manifolds (Oxford Mathematical Monographs)
Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)

items.title: The pullback foliation under a transverse map
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a regular foliation of $M$ of codimension $q$, let $N$ be a smooth manifold and $f:N\to M$ a smooth map transverse to $F$. Put $D_x^*:=(df_x)^{-1}\bigl(D_{f(x)}\bigr)$, where $D=TF$. Then $D^*$ is a smooth rank-$(\dim N-q)$ distribution on $N$, it is integrable, and the associated regular foliation $f^*F$ has as its leaves the connected components of the preimages $f^{-1}(L)$ of the leaves $L$ of $F$. Each leaf of $f^*F$ is mapped by $f$ into a leaf of $F$.
items.strategy: In a foliation chart on $M$, let $y:U\to\mathbb R^q$ be the transverse-coordinate submersion, so $D|_U=\ker dy$. Transversality implies $g=y\circ f$ is a submersion on $f^{-1}(U)$, because the induced map $T_xN\to T_{f(x)}M/D_{f(x)}$ is surjective. Thus $D_x^*=\ker dg_x$ has constant rank $\dim N-q$, and the constant-rank kernel theorem makes it a smooth subbundle. Submersion coordinates give local integral plaques as connected level sets of $g$, proving integrability directly without extending arbitrary sections along a possibly noninjective $f$ to ambient vector fields. On overlaps these plaques agree because they are precisely the local connected preimages of the original plaques; the foliation/distribution correspondence supplies the associated regular foliation. A connected leaf preimage, equipped with its pulled-back plaque topology, is assembled from these plaques; every connected integral manifold maps into a single leaf and conversely each such connected component is an integral manifold. Maximality therefore gives exactly the asserted leaves. The pullback and quotient bundle constructions identify the same kernel as $TN\to f^*TM\to f^*(TM/D)$. Only the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used.

references.title: Danny Calegari, Foliations and the Geometry of 3-Manifolds (Oxford Mathematical Monographs)
Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)

items.title: The quotient foliation under a free and properly discontinuous foliated action
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\Gamma$ be a group acting on a smooth manifold $M$ by
diffeomorphisms, and suppose the action is **free and properly discontinuous**:
$\gamma\cdot x=x$ implies $\gamma=e$ for all $x\in M$, and for every compact
subset $K\subseteq M$ the set
$\{\gamma\in\Gamma:\gamma K\cap K\neq\varnothing\}$ is finite. Let $F$ be a
regular foliation of $M$ preserved by $\Gamma$, so every $\gamma$ maps leaves
onto leaves, with tangent distribution $D=TF$. Then:

1. $M/\Gamma$ carries a unique smooth structure for which the orbit map
   $\pi:M\to M/\Gamma$ is a local diffeomorphism, and with this structure $\pi$
   is a covering map;
2. there is a unique regular foliation $F/\Gamma$ on $M/\Gamma$ whose leaves are
   the images $\pi(L)$ of the leaves of $F$, and its codimension equals
   $\operatorname{codim}F$;
3. the tangent distribution of $F/\Gamma$ is $d\pi(D)$.
items.strategy: Proper discontinuity gives at each point a neighbourhood meeting none of its nonidentity translates, so the orbit map is a covering and the action is a covering-space action. Hausdorff and second countability follow from the closed orbit relation: for compact $K$ only finitely many $\gamma$ satisfy $\gamma K\cap K\neq\varnothing$, and distinct orbits are separated by invariant open sets built from finitely many such $\gamma$. Smooth structure: charts of $M$ composed with local inverses of $\pi$; two local sections over a common connected open set differ there by a single group element, so transitions are smooth restrictions and the atlas is well defined; uniqueness follows because any smooth structure making $\pi$ a local diffeomorphism is compatible with this atlas. Foliation: the pushforward distribution $d\pi(D)$ is well defined, smooth of rank $\dim M-\operatorname{codim}F$ and integrable, and its maximal integral manifolds are exactly the images $\pi(L)$ of the leaves; this gives the unique regular foliation $F/\Gamma$ with the stated codimension.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)
Danny Calegari, Foliations and the Geometry of 3-Manifolds (Oxford Mathematical Monographs)

items.title: The suspension foliation of a representation of the fundamental group
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $B$ be a connected smooth manifold with base point $b_0$, let $F$ be a smooth manifold, let $p:\widetilde B\to B$ be a universal cover and let $\rho:\pi_1(B,b_0)\to\operatorname{Diff}(F)$ be a homomorphism into the diffeomorphism group of $F$. Using the isomorphism $\pi_1(B,b_0)\cong\operatorname{Deck}(\widetilde B\to B)$, let $\pi_1(B,b_0)$ act on $\widetilde B\times F$ diagonally by $$\gamma\cdot(x,y):=\bigl(\gamma\cdot x,\rho(\gamma)(y)\bigr).$$ This is a covering-space action by diffeomorphisms, so the quotient $M_\rho:=(\widetilde B\times F)/\pi_1(B,b_0)$ is a smooth manifold, the orbit map $\pi$ is a covering, and the product foliation of $\widetilde B\times F$ by the leaves $\widetilde B\times\{y\}$, which is invariant under the action, descends by the quotient-foliation proposition to a regular foliation $F_\rho$ of $M_\rho$ of codimension $\dim F$, the **suspension foliation** of $\rho$.
items.strategy: Verify the covering-space action: given $(x,y)$, choose $U\subseteq\widetilde B$ with $\gamma U\cap U=\varnothing$ for all nonidentity $\gamma$ (the deck action of a universal cover is such an action by the deck-group lemma), then $(U\times F)\cap\gamma(U\times F)=\varnothing$ because the first coordinate already separates. Freeness is clear from $\gamma x=x$. The product foliation is invariant because $\gamma\cdot(\widetilde B\times\{y\})=\widetilde B\times\{\rho(\gamma)y\}$. Apply the quotient-foliation proposition to obtain the manifold, the covering orbit map and the descended foliation. This is the standard suspension of a flat bundle construction; no topology on the arrow set of a groupoid is involved.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)
Danny Calegari, Foliations and the Geometry of 3-Manifolds (Oxford Mathematical Monographs)

items.title: Suspension holonomy is the germ of the represented monodromy action
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. In the suspension of the representation $\rho$ let $\gamma:[0,1]\to B$ be a loop at $b_0$ with class $[\gamma]\in\pi_1(B,b_0)$, let $\tilde x\in\widetilde B$ lie over $b_0$, let $\tilde x_\gamma$ be the lift of $\gamma$ with $\tilde x_\gamma(0)=\tilde x$, so $\tilde x_\gamma(1)=[\gamma]\cdot\tilde x$, and let $y\in F$. Then $a(t):=\pi(\tilde x_\gamma(t),y)$ is a leafwise path of $F_\rho$, and its holonomy germ between the local transversals $T=\pi(\{\tilde x\}\times F)$ at the start and the corresponding slice at the end is the germ at $y$ of $\rho([\gamma])^{-1}$: $$h_a=\text{germ}_y\bigl(\rho([\gamma])^{-1}\bigr).$$ Moreover the leaf $L_y=\pi(\widetilde B\times\{y\})$ is diffeomorphic to $\widetilde B/K_y$ with $K_y=\{\gamma:\rho(\gamma)y=y\}$, and under $\pi_1(L_y)\cong K_y$ the holonomy representation of the leaf is $\gamma\mapsto\rho(\gamma)^{-1}$.
items.strategy: Work on $\widetilde B\times F$, where the product foliation has the straight leaves $\widetilde B\times\{y\}$; the slice $\{\tilde x\}\times F$ is a local transversal because $\pi$ is a covering and the two directions are complementary. Transporting the slice along $t\mapsto(\tilde x_\gamma(t),y)$ keeps the $F$-coordinate, so at $t=1$ the point $(\tilde x_\gamma(1),y)=(\gamma\cdot\tilde x,y)$ is identified in $M_\rho$ with $(\tilde x,\rho(\gamma)^{-1}y)$; hence the germ is $\rho([\gamma])^{-1}$ (with the action convention displayed). For the leaf: $\pi$ restricts to a bijection $\widetilde B/K_y\to L_y$ that is a local diffeomorphism, and $K_y$ acts as a covering-space action, so $\pi_1(L_y)\cong K_y$ by the deck-group theorem; the same transport computation gives the restriction of $\rho(\,\cdot\,)^{-1}$.

references.title: Danny Calegari, Foliations and the Geometry of 3-Manifolds (Oxford Mathematical Monographs)
Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)

items.title: Holonomy is a germ, not a globally defined return map
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. The holonomy of a leafwise path is a germ of a local diffeomorphism between local transversals, not a globally defined return map: a representative is defined only on some open neighbourhood of the base point in the transversal, and different representatives of the same germ may differ arbitrarily far from that point. The Poincaré return map of a periodic orbit of a flow is the special case in which the first-return construction defines a map on a fixed section; that is additional structure, not part of the general definition. Statements about 'the' return map along a leaf loop must therefore be read as statements about the holonomy germ.
items.strategy: Point at the construction and its certificates: the finite chain in the construction of the germ is defined on a neighbourhood of the base point only, and chain independence compares germs, so nothing defines values away from the base point. The source's presentation starts from the Poincaré return map as motivation and then replaces it by germs precisely because the return map requires a chosen section and a first-return time. No proof obligation beyond the cited construction items.

references.title: Leiden NCG seminar, Noncommutative Geometry of Foliations (2023 seminar notes)
Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)

items.title: Holonomy and monodromy groupoids need not be Hausdorff
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. The monodromy groupoid and the holonomy groupoid of a foliation carry smooth structures making them étale Lie groupoids, and they can fail to be Hausdorff even though the foliated manifold is Hausdorff; the two failures are independent, in the sense that either groupoid can be Hausdorff while the other is not. This item records the phenomenon; it is not proved here, and no topology on the groupoid arrow sets is constructed on this page. The groupoid definitions of this page are set-theoretic and make no Hausdorffness assertion.
items.strategy: Recorded, not proved here. The phenomenon is stated in the sources, which also give a mechanism: a non-contractible loop in a leaf approached by contractible loops in nearby leaves makes elements of the monodromy groupoid converge both to a nontrivial arrow and to a unit, which is incompatible with Hausdorffness. A self-contained example (Reeb foliation of the three-sphere; the foliation of the complement of the origin in $\mathbb{R}^3$ by the fibres of a projection) would require constructing the étale topology on the arrow set, which this page deliberately does not do; the recorded statement suffices for the design's purpose of preventing a silent Hausdorffness assumption.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)
Leiden NCG seminar, Noncommutative Geometry of Foliations (2023 seminar notes)

title: Foliation Holonomy and the Holonomy Groupoid — Examples

items.title: The Kronecker foliation of the torus has dense leaves and trivial leaf holonomy
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $\alpha\in\mathbb R\setminus\mathbb Q$ and let $F_\alpha$ be the linear foliation of $\mathbb T^2=\mathbb R^2/\mathbb Z^2$ whose leaves are the images of the lines $t\mapsto[p+t(1,\alpha)]$. Then every leaf is dense in $\mathbb T^2$, every leaf is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb R$, and the holonomy group of every point is trivial: for every leaf $L$ and $x\in L$ the holonomy representation $\rho_x:\pi_1(L,x)\to\operatorname{Diff}_x(T)$ has trivial domain $\pi_1(L,x)=0$, so every leaf loop has the identity holonomy germ. In particular this foliation has dense leaves while its holonomy is as trivial as that of a product foliation.
items.strategy: Density: it suffices to treat the leaf through $[0]$. The fractional parts of the multiples of $\alpha$ form a dense subgroup of $\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$: for $\varepsilon>0$ the pigeonhole principle applied to $0,\alpha,\dots,N\alpha$ with $1/N<\varepsilon$ produces $\beta=k\alpha$ with $0<\beta<\varepsilon$ in the circle, and the multiples of $\beta$ form an $\varepsilon$-net; then for any target $(u,v)$ choose $t=u+mk$ with $m\beta$ close to $v-\alpha u$. Every other leaf is a translate, and translations are homeomorphisms, so all leaves are dense. Leaf structure: $t\mapsto[(t,\alpha t)]$ is a continuous bijection onto the leaf (injectivity uses irrationality of $\alpha$) and an injective immersion; in flow-box coordinates of the linear foliation it is a straight-line graph, hence a local diffeomorphism onto the leaf with its leaf structure, so by uniqueness of the maximal integral manifold structure the leaf is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb R$. Hence $\pi_1(L,x)=0$ because $\mathbb R$ is convex, and the holonomy representation is trivial; homotopy invariance identifies every leaf-loop germ with the identity germ.

references.title: Danny Calegari, Foliations and the Geometry of 3-Manifolds (Oxford Mathematical Monographs)
Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)
Leiden NCG seminar, Noncommutative Geometry of Foliations (2023 seminar notes)

items.title: The Möbius band's central leaf has reflection holonomy
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $\mathrm{Mob}=(\mathbb R\times(-1,1))/\mathbb Z$ be the smooth Möbius band, with the action $k\cdot(t,x)=(t+k,(-1)^kx)$, and let $F$ be the foliation whose leaves are the images of the horizontal segments $\mathbb R\times\{x\}$; the projection $[t,x]\mapsto[t]$ is a circle bundle to which $F$ is transverse. Then the middle leaf $L_{\mathrm{mid}}=\pi(\mathbb R\times\{0\})$ is diffeomorphic to $S^1$ and its holonomy group at every point is $\mathbb Z/2$: the generator of $\pi_1(L_{\mathrm{mid}})\cong\mathbb Z$ has holonomy germ the reflection $x\mapsto-x$ of the transversal, and its square has trivial germ. Every other leaf is diffeomorphic to $S^1$ (it wraps twice around the band) and has trivial holonomy group.
items.strategy: The band is the suspension of the representation $\rho:\mathbb Z\to\operatorname{Diff}((-1,1))$, $k\mapsto(x\mapsto(-1)^kx)$, over $B=S^1$, so the suspension proposition applies: the leaf through $(0,0)$ is the image of $\mathbb R\times\{0\}$, and the base loop $\gamma$ of $S^1$ has leaf path from $[0,0]$ to $[1,0]=[0,0]$ whose holonomy germ is $\rho(1)^{-1}:x\mapsto-x$, a nontrivial involution; the isotropy proposition identifies the holonomy group with the cyclic group generated by this germ, of order $2$. For $x\ne0$ the stabilizer of $x$ under the action is $2\mathbb Z$, so the corresponding leaf is $\mathbb R/2\mathbb Z\cong S^1$ and the class generating its fundamental group is the double of the core loop, whose holonomy germ is $\rho(2)^{-1}=\mathrm{id}$; hence the holonomy group is trivial.

references.title: Leiden NCG seminar, Noncommutative Geometry of Foliations (2023 seminar notes)
Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)

items.title: The suspension of a circle diffeomorphism: leaves and return germs
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $f:S^1\to S^1$ be a diffeomorphism and let $M_f=(\mathbb R\times S^1)/\mathbb Z$ with $k\cdot(t,y)=(t+k,f^k(y))$; let $F_f$ be the suspension foliation of the representation $\rho(k)=f^k$ over $B=S^1$. Then: (i) the leaf $L_y$ through $[0,y]$ is diffeomorphic to $S^1$ when the orbit of $y$ under $f$ is periodic, and to $\mathbb R$ otherwise; (ii) if $y$ has minimal period $k\ge1$, the leaf loop $a(t)=[(t,y)]$, $t\in[0,k]$, generates $\pi_1(L_y)\cong\mathbb Z$ and has holonomy germ at $[0,y]$ equal to the germ of $f^{-k}$ at $y$, so the holonomy group of $L_y$ is the cyclic group generated by that germ; (iii) in particular for $f$ the identity the foliation is the product foliation of $\mathbb T^2$ by circles and all holonomy germs are trivial, while for a rotation by $2\pi p/q$ every leaf is a circle and every holonomy germ is trivial.
items.strategy: (i) $\pi$ restricted to $\mathbb R\times\{y\}$ factors through the period group $K_y=\{k:f^k(y)=y\}$ and is a diffeomorphism onto $L_y$ with $\mathbb R/K_y$, which is $S^1$ for a nontrivial period group and $\mathbb R$ otherwise. (ii) The path $a$ is closed exactly when $f^k(y)=y$; the suspension-holonomy proposition gives the germ $\rho(k)^{-1}=f^{-k}$ at $y$, and the isotropy proposition identifies the holonomy group of the leaf with the image of its fundamental group, which is generated by this class. (iii) For $f=\mathrm{id}$ the total space is $\mathbb T^2$ with the product foliation and every $K_y=\mathbb Z$ acts trivially on the fibre, so all germs are trivial; for a rotation of order $q$, $f^q=\mathrm{id}$ and the generator has trivial germ.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)
Danny Calegari, Foliations and the Geometry of 3-Manifolds (Oxford Mathematical Monographs)

items.title: The flat-bundle foliation from a linear representation
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $A\in\mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb R)$ and let $M_A=(\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n)/\mathbb Z$ with $k\cdot(t,v)=(t+k,A^kv)$, a suspension of the linear representation $\rho(k)=A^k$ over $B=S^1$; let $F_A$ be the suspension foliation of $M_A$. Then: (i) $M_A\to S^1$, $[t,v]\mapsto[t]$, is a smooth fibre bundle with fibre $\mathbb R^n$ and locally constant transition functions (a flat vector bundle); (ii) if $Av=v$, then the leaf through $[0,v]$ is a circle and the leaf loop $a(t)=[(t,v)]$, $t\in[0,1]$, has holonomy germ the germ of $A^{-1}$ at $v$; for $A$ diagonal with all eigenvalues different from $1$, the leaf through the origin is a circle whose holonomy group is generated by the germ of $A^{-1}$ at $0$ and is nontrivial whenever $A\ne I$; (iii) the foliation $F_A$ is transverse to the fibres of the bundle projection.
items.strategy: (i) Use the two standard charts of $S^1$ and the trivializations $[t,v]\mapsto([t],v)$ over each chart; on the overlap the change of coordinates is the locally constant map $v\mapsto A^{\pm1}v$, so $M_A$ is a flat fibre bundle over the circle. (ii) The leaf through $[0,v]$ is the image of $\mathbb R\times\{v\}$; it is a circle when $Av=v$, and the suspension-holonomy proposition computes the holonomy of the closed leaf path as the germ of $\rho(1)^{-1}=A^{-1}$; the isotropy proposition turns that germ into the holonomy group of the leaf. (iii) The leaf directions are the $\mathbb R$ directions and the fibre directions are the $\mathbb R^n$ directions, which are complementary and of the correct dimensions, so transversality is a pointwise linear fact at every $[t,v]$.

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)
Danny Calegari, Foliations and the Geometry of 3-Manifolds (Oxford Mathematical Monographs)

items.title: A nontransverse pullback need not reproduce the rank of a foliation
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. The following inference is false: for an arbitrary smooth map $f:N\to M$ and a regular foliation $F$ of $M$, the inverse-image spaces $D_t^*:=(df_t)^{-1}(T_{f(t)}F)$ form a smooth distribution of constant rank $\dim N-\operatorname{codim}F$ and define a regular pullback foliation whose leaves are the connected components of leaf preimages. Counterexample: let $M=\mathbb R^2$ with the horizontal foliation, $N=\mathbb R$, and $f(t)=(0,t^2)$. Since $df_t(v)=(0,2tv)$ and $T_{f(t)}F=\mathbb R\times\{0\}$, one has $D_t^*=\{0\}$ for $t\ne0$ but $D_0^*=T_0\mathbb R$. Thus the rank jumps from $0$ to $1$ at $0$, so $D^*$ is not a regular distribution. The map is transverse to $F$ for $t\ne0$ and nontransverse at $0$. This refutes the rank and regular-distribution inference without the transversality hypothesis.
items.strategy: Use the inverse-image convention of [[prop-pullback-foliation-under-a-transverse-map]]: $D_t^*$ consists of tangent vectors $v$ such that $df_t(v)$ lies in the horizontal line. For $f(t)=(0,t^2)$, this condition is $2tv=0$. If $t\ne0$ it forces $v=0$, whereas at $t=0$ every tangent vector qualifies. Hence rank is nonconstant and the inverse-image spaces cannot form a smooth vector subbundle of $T\mathbb R$. For $t\ne0$ the vertical image of $df_t$ and the horizontal leaf tangent span $\mathbb R^2$; at $0$ their sum is only the horizontal line. The horizontal-leaf preimages are finite sets, so their connected components are points; their zero-dimensional decomposition cannot have the displayed rank-jumping tangent spaces. The construction uses no choice beyond the standing foliation-interface premise.

references.title: Leiden NCG seminar, Noncommutative Geometry of Foliations (2023 seminar notes, complete 53-page PDF)
Danny Calegari, Foliations and the Geometry of 3-Manifolds (Oxford Mathematical Monographs; author-hosted PDF)

items.title: Two nonhomotopic leaf loops can have the same holonomy germ
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). The
following inference is false: two leaf loops with the same holonomy germ are
leafwise homotopic relative to endpoints, so that the holonomy groupoid would
coincide with the monodromy groupoid.

**Counterexample.** In the Möbius band foliation constructed below, the middle leaf has
$\pi_1(L_{\mathrm{mid}})\cong\mathbb Z$ generated by the core loop $\gamma$,
whose holonomy germ is the reflection $x\mapsto-x$. The double $2\gamma$ is not
null-homotopic in the leaf, yet its holonomy germ is the square of the
reflection, that is, the identity germ, as is the germ of the constant loop.
Hence the constant loop and $2\gamma$ are nonhomotopic relative to endpoints and
have the same holonomy germ, and the kernel of the holonomy representation is
the nontrivial subgroup $2\mathbb Z\le\mathbb Z$; the natural map
$\operatorname{Mon}(F)\to\operatorname{Hol}(F)$ is not injective in general.
items.strategy: Use the previous example: multiplicativity of holonomy germs gives $h_{2\gamma}=h_\gamma\circ h_\gamma=r\circ r=\mathrm{id}$, while $2\gamma\ne 0$ in $\pi_1(L_{\mathrm{mid}})\cong\mathbb Z$; the constant loop has identity germ and is null-homotopic. The two loops therefore have equal germs and unequal classes, so the stated inference fails and the two groupoids are genuinely different quotients of the path groupoid.

references.title: Leiden NCG seminar, Noncommutative Geometry of Foliations (2023 seminar notes)
Eckhard Meinrenken, Lie Groupoids and Lie Algebroids, lecture notes (University of Toronto MAT1341, Fall 2017)
